ruling.recommended_action: Refund SGD 3.07 to the rider by Ryde voucher for the unexcused detour segment (RD-2); no account action.
ruling.reasoning:
This is a RydeTAXI metered trip (F7: base $3.90 + distance $30.46 for 21.60 km + time $9.10 + waiting $0.11 + platform $1.47 = $45.04), so extra distance is billable and the metered branch of RD-2 applies. The trace settles that one off-route segment exists [F3] and that no traffic incident qualifies under RD-4(a) [F15]; the East Coast Parkway speed-band record [F12] is corroborative only, since RD-4(b) does not exempt on its own, so RD-4 gives no relief here [F3][F12][F15][RD-1][RD-4].

The rider's message needs reading carefully. The driver asked at 09:17: "Jam on East Coast Parkway is building up ahead, want me to take another way?" [F8], and the rider answered at 09:18: "Just take whichever way is faster lah, I'm late." [F9] — before the segment start, in a complete and fully timestamped chat [F10]. That is an agreement, but its scope is a general route choice only: it covers a route chosen to get to the destination, and it does not cover an errand or loop of the driver's own [F9][RD-5]. Consent scope is read from the words, and the words here do not name any road or area, so what was authorised is a route that is actually faster [F9][RD-5].

The record shows this segment was not such a route: 4.04 km driven where the optimal route covers 1.86 km, up to 1027 m off the optimal route, and the trip finished at 35.4 min against a 25.2 min estimate with +2.3 km over optimal in total [F1][F2][F3]. The driver's own post-trip statement — "the rider said any faster way was fine, so I went round" [F11] — is not rider consent (G11) and confirms the loop was the driver's own choice, not a rider-named stop [F11][RD-3][RD-5]. The extra kilometres of this driver-chosen loop therefore fall outside the general consent and are refundable [F3][F9][F11][RD-2][RD-5]. I note openly that the driver's premise of congestion on the replaced stretch was borne out by the speed-band record [F12]; that is why confidence is held at 0.7 rather than treating the segment as an obvious driver errand.

The rider also queries the waiting fee [F5]. On a RydeTAXI trip, in-trip stop-and-wait time is charged by the meter's waiting units and is not refunded under RD-3(c); the $0.11 (0.4 min × $0.26/min) is meter time and stands [F5][F7][RD-3]. The driver has no upheld route dispute in the last 90 days (F18: route upheld = 0), so RD-6 is not triggered and no account flag is added [F18][RD-6].

Amount (metered refund under RD-2): only the extra kilometres of the unexcused segment are refunded; the flat excess-distance line [F4] is a data artefact and is not used. 2.18 km × $1.4102/km = $3.07424, rounded to $3.07, where $1.4102/km is this trip's distance fare ÷ distance km ($30.46 ÷ 21.60 km) [F3][F4][F7][RD-2].

Safety screen: I read the complaint, both chat messages and the driver statement [F8][F9][F11]. They are a route discussion and a fare complaint; no threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation appears. Safety concern: none.

The segment driven (4.04 km where the optimal route covers 1.86 km, up to 1027 m off route; trip +2.3 km / 12% distance and +10.2 min over estimate) was not the faster route authorised [F1][F2][F3][F8][F9], and the driver's post-trip statement 'so I went round' [F11] is the driver's own account, not rider consent (G11).
